instantiated_cells.justification: Section 86113(b) requires the lobbyist to submit a periodic report within two weeks following the end of each calendar quarter, not annually.
The statute specifies quarterly reporting (within two weeks after each calendar quarter), not monthly reporting.
The law sets a quarterly cadence and does not provide an alternate 'other' frequency for the lobbyist periodic report.
A lobbyist must provide the original periodic report to the employer or lobbying firm within two weeks following the end of each calendar quarter, implying quarterly reporting.
The lobbyist periodic report is due after each calendar quarter rather than on a semi-annual schedule.
The lobbyist periodic report is tied to calendar quarters, not tri-annual legislative-calendar deadlines.

Lobbyists must report all activity expenses during the reporting period, and when activity expenses are reported the law requires the date, amount, beneficiary, and description of the benefit (itemization).
Section 86113(b) makes the lobbyist periodic report due within two weeks following the end of each calendar quarter, i.e., quarterly.
The lobbyist periodic report must contain activity expenses and certain contributions, but the statute does not require identifying specific bills, executive actions, or positions.
Section 86113 requires a lobbyist to report activity expenses and certain contributions, while client payments are reported by lobbying firms under § 86114(a)(2), not by the lobbyist.
The lobbyist periodic report requirements listed in § 86113 do not include disclosing lobbying contacts or communications.
The lobbyist report requires itemized activity expenses but does not require allocating expenditures by issue or bill.
Neither § 86113 nor § 86112 requires the lobbyist to disclose general issues or subjects lobbied as part of the lobbyist periodic report.
The lobbyist periodic report is limited to activity expenses and specified contributions and does not require reporting general subjects of lobbying.
Activity expenses, which lobbyists must report under § 86113(a)(1), include gifts and other forms of compensation benefiting officials, capturing items such as gifts and entertainment.

The lobbyist periodic report covers 'activity expenses' benefiting specified officials, but it does not require reporting the lobbyist’s other indirect lobbying costs not fitting the 'activity expense' definition.
Lobbyists must file a periodic report of all activity expenses and those expenses must be itemized with date, amount, beneficiary, payee, and description.
Section 86113 does not require the lobbyist periodic report to include the lobbyist’s address or phone number (those appear in certification/registration requirements, not the periodic report).
The lobbyist periodic report does not require disclosure of bills/actions discussed or positions taken—only activity expenses and certain contributions.

The lobbyist periodic report requirements do not include disclosure of the principal’s business nature; those details are in registration statements for firms/employers, not the lobbyist periodic report.
Section 86113 does not require a lobbyist periodic report to list the address/phone number of principals represented.
The lobbyist periodic report described in § 86113 contains activity expenses and certain contributions and does not require listing all principals represented.
No provision in § 86113 requires a lobbyist to identify bills or legislation IDs in the periodic report.
The lobbyist periodic report requires reporting activity expenses and certain contributions but does not require reporting compensation received by the lobbyist as a direct lobbying cost.
Section 86113 requires a report of activity expenses rather than a report of the lobbyist’s total expenditures toward lobbying overall.

Lobbyists must file itemized activity expense information (date, amount, beneficiary, description), even though compensation is not required, meeting at least the 'itemized spending reports' component.

Because 'activity expense' includes expenses benefiting an official or a member of the official’s immediate family, and lobbyists must report all activity expenses, spending benefiting household/immediate family members is reportable.
When activity expenses are reported, the statute requires the date and amount of each expense and a description and beneficiary, which is itemized rather than lump-sum.
